metric_definitions.recall@k: gold chunks in the top k / gold chunks
metric_definitions.precision@k: gold chunks in the top k / k, even when fewer than k come back
metric_definitions.wrong_evidence: questions where a hard negative ranks above at least one gold chunk in the retrieved list (a gold chunk not retrieved ranks below all), or is cited anywhere in the raw answer / questions with hard negatives; by_relation counts a question under each hard-negative label that triggered, over the questions with a negative of that label; share_of_wrong is the share of wrong questions that label triggered (H3)
metric_definitions.exact_match: share of questions whose filter companies and periods both equal the labels
metric_definitions.companies_match: share of questions whose filter companies equal the tickers label
metric_definitions.periods_match: share of questions whose filter periods equal the fiscal_periods label
metric_definitions.filter_excluded_gold: gold chunks whose filing the filter excluded, summed over questions
metric_definitions.structural_citation_validity: cited chunk IDs that were among the retrieved chunks / cited chunk IDs, counted over every sentence of the raw answer, kept or dropped; null when nothing was cited
metric_definitions.dropped_share: sentences dropped by citation enforcement / sentences in the raw answers
metric_definitions.status: the answer's status line: answered, declined, not_found; no_status if the line was missing; refused if the API refused
metric_definitions.latency_ms: p50 and p95 per stage, by linear interpolation between the closest ranks; embed and retrieval (embed plus search) count only questions whose query embedding was made in this run; generation is each answer call's API latency when it was made, also for an answer replayed from the cache
metric_definitions.cost_usd: from the token counts each API reported and the header's dated price table; Voyage at list price, before any free allowance
metric_definitions.interval: percentile bootstrap 95% interval over 10000 resamples of the cell's questions, with replacement; each interval's generator is seeded by the header's seed and the interval's set, arm, class and metric; for a ratio, resamples with a zero denominator are left out and 'resamples' counts the rest
metric_definitions.directional: the cell has fewer than 10 questions in the scored split (research plan)
metric_definitions.judged: scored by an LLM judge, uncalibrated: no judge has been checked against hand scores yet; each metric runs 3 times as independent calls; a question's score is the mean of its runs that produced a value and its spread the highest run minus the lowest; a cell's mean is over its questions' scores, run_means is the cell mean within each run, spread is the highest run mean minus the lowest, and the interval resamples the questions' scores; a run with no value (skipped, undefined, or an unusable judge reply, which 'errors' counts) is left out
metric_definitions.faithfulness: Ragas faithfulness: statements in the kept sentences (citation markers removed) that the judge infers from the retrieved chunks / statements; skipped when no sentence was kept; no value when the judge finds no statements
metric_definitions.answer_relevancy: Ragas answer relevancy: mean cosine similarity (Voyage query embeddings) between the question and 3 questions the judge writes from the shown answer (citation markers removed), 0 if the judge calls every one noncommittal; skipped for an empty answer
metric_definitions.citation_support: kept sentences whose cited chunks, together, support every claim in them, per the judge / kept sentences; skipped when no sentence was kept
metric_definitions.judged_cost_usd: what judging cost (OpenAI judge calls plus Voyage embeddings for answer relevancy), over all runs; an evaluation cost, kept out of the operational cost_usd, which is what answering a question costs
metric_definitions.judge_usage: judge tokens over all runs as OpenAI reported them, replayed calls included: input_tokens includes cached_input_tokens and cache_write_tokens; output_tokens includes reasoning_tokens, which are shown separately and billed as output
metric_definitions.decline_correct: decline records: 1 if the judge finds the answer declined to advise
metric_definitions.not_found_correct: unanswerable records: 1 if the judge finds the answer said the filings lack the evidence without stating or guessing the fact

questions.question: Beyond lost direct sales, what knock-on competitive effects of U.S.-China export controls and trade tensions do NVIDIA, AMD and Intel describe in their latest 10-Ks?

answer.text:
NVIDIA: It says export controls have encouraged customers outside China and other impacted regions to "design out" certain U.S. semiconductors, and have encouraged overseas governments to ask customers to buy from competitors rather than NVIDIA or other U.S. firms [0001045810-26-000021:0045]. It says the controls may increase investment in foreign competitors, which are less likely to be restricted by U.S. controls [0001045810-26-000021:0045]. It says the possibility of further controls has reduced demand for its products and benefited competitors whose alternatives are less likely to be restricted [0001045810-26-000021:0041]. It says licensing requirements benefit certain competitors and encourage customers in China, the Middle East and other regions to pursue alternatives, including suppliers based in China, Europe and Israel [0001045810-26-000021:0043]. It also says the controls have a disproportionate impact on NVIDIA and may disadvantage it against competitors whose chips fall outside the controls [0001045810-26-000021:0044]. It adds that the Chinese government has encouraged customers to buy from China-based competitors and discouraged them from buying NVIDIA's data center products [0001045810-26-000021:0045]. It says demand may fall in markets beyond China, such as Europe, Latin America and Southeast Asia, and that the controls can leave it with excess inventory and purchase obligations, as it recently experienced with the H20 [0001045810-26-000021:0045]. It also says the controls have disrupted its supply chain and distribution channels, and that they can affect non-data-center products and markets outside China [0001045810-26-000021:0041].
AMD: It says export controls have encouraged customers in China and other controlled markets to pursue alternatives to U.S. semiconductors, and that it may be at a competitive disadvantage if its competitors are not subject to the same restrictions [0000002488-26-000018:0044]. It says limits on China sales could weaken its position against domestic Chinese competitors and other companies not subject to the same restrictions, and that it could lose market position [0000002488-26-000018:0043]. It says any U.S. government request for a percentage of revenue from licensed MI308 China sales could harm its competitive position and benefit competitors not subject to such arrangements [0000002488-26-000018:0043]. It says government incentives to competitors could strengthen their relative position [0000002488-26-000018:0044]. It says additions to the Entity List could force it to suspend purchases from suppliers or sales to customers, disrupting its supply chain [0000002488-26-000018:0045]. It also says tariffs could raise customers' costs and lead them to delay or cancel AI infrastructure investments [0000002488-26-000018:0044].
Intel: It says trade tensions have increased tariffs and trade restrictions, affected customer ordering patterns, and in some instances reduced its sales [0000050863-26-000011:0072]. It says sustained tensions could lead to decoupling of global trade networks, making it harder to sell in or access some markets [0000050863-26-000011:0072]. It says a number of semiconductor companies in China, including SMIC, are investing heavily, often with Chinese government support, in advanced technologies to develop competing products [0000050863-26-000011:0072]. It also says China has responded with its own restrictions, including licensing requirements on critical minerals [0000050863-26-000011:0072].

questions.question: How do the climate and environmental-regulation risks described by NVIDIA, AMD and Intel in their latest 10-Ks differ, given that two are fabless and one runs its own fabs?

answer.text:
It says environmental regulations on materials, processes, air quality and wastewater may impede its ability to manufacture or to expand or modify its manufacturing capability [0000050863-26-000011:0087]. It notes that perfluorocarbons used in semiconductor manufacturing have historically made up a large portion of its direct greenhouse gas emissions [0000050863-26-000011:0087]. New limits on these compounds or other emissions could require it to install abatement equipment, buy carbon offsets or alter production processes [0000050863-26-000011:0087]. Intel also says regulation of PFAS, which are found in parts, components and process chemicals, could matter because there are limited feasible alternatives [0000050863-26-000011:0087]. It adds that expanding manufacturing capacity could magnify the impact of future laws [0000050863-26-000011:0087]. Its wider environmental, health and safety risk factor covers regulatory penalties, remediation obligations, suspension of production and changes to its manufacturing and assembly and test processes [0000050863-26-000011:0086].
It says its manufacturing suppliers may face higher costs from climate-related expectations on abatement equipment, renewable energy and production processes, and that these compliance costs may be passed on to AMD as indirect costs [0000002488-26-000018:0041]. AMD also expects higher energy costs from carbon pricing on utilities or from having to buy more renewable energy than planned [0000002488-26-000018:0050]. Its physical climate risk includes natural disasters and extreme weather disrupting its suppliers, and it cites an April 2024 earthquake in Taiwan, where its third-party wafer foundries are located [0000002488-26-000018:0059]. AMD does describe direct environmental exposure of a different kind: it has been named a responsible party at three Superfund sites in Sunnyvale, California [0000002488-26-000018:0018]. It also cites EU and China restrictions on lead and other materials in electronic products, and ENERGY STAR-based market entry rules that could exclude some of its products from certain markets [0000002488-26-000018:0050].
It cites extreme heat and wind in Northern California that may cause power safety shut-offs affecting its Santa Clara headquarters offices and data centers [0001045810-26-000021:0033]. It says climate change and its effect on its supply chain and critical infrastructure may raise its costs to maintain or resume operations [0001045810-26-000021:0033]. These include costs tied to changes in manufacturing processes or raw materials procurement and compliance costs that suppliers or customers pass on to NVIDIA [0001045810-26-000021:0033]. It separately notes its dependence on supply from overseas partners, especially in Taiwan and South Korea [0001045810-26-000021:0046]. It also flags concerns about the high absolute energy requirements of its GPUs [0001045810-26-000021:0033].
NVIDIA and AMD say shortages or regulatory limits could impair customers' ability to expand data center capacity and consume their products [0001045810-26-000021:0033][0000002488-26-000018:0041].

questions.question: How does the share price shape the talent-retention risk that NVIDIA, AMD and Intel each describe in their latest 10-K risk factors?

answer.text:
NVIDIA says that in times of stock price volatility, as it has experienced in the past and may experience in the future, the retentive value of its stock-based compensation may decrease [0001045810-26-000021:0037]. It adds that competition for talent drives up costs in the form of cash and stock-based compensation [0001045810-26-000021:0037].
AMD says it uses share-based incentive awards to help attract, retain and motivate executives and qualified employees [0000002488-26-000018:0060]. If the value of those awards does not appreciate with the price of its common stock, or if share-based compensation ceases to be viewed as a valuable benefit, its ability to attract, retain and motivate employees could be affected, which could harm its results of operations [0000002488-26-000018:0060]. AMD also notes that stock price fluctuations could affect the value of its equity compensation and thereby its ability to recruit and retain employees [0000002488-26-000018:0060]. It further says that a substantial increase in the value of its stock awards could create great personal wealth for executives and key talent and affect its ability to retain them [0000002488-26-000018:0060].
Intel says it uses share-based awards, such as RSUs, and performance-based cash incentive awards to attract, retain and motivate qualified employees [0000050863-26-000011:0082]. It states that sustained declines in its stock price, or lower stock price performance relative to competitors in recent years, have reduced the retention value of its share-based awards, which has impacted the competitiveness of its compensation [0000050863-26-000011:0082].

questions.question: How did AI accelerator demand show up in each company's segment results in its latest 10-K, and what accelerator-related inventory charges offset it?

answer.text:
AMD said demand for its data center AI accelerators was strong in 2025 as large hyperscale customers, OEMs and ODMs deployed AMD Instinct MI350X Series GPUs [0000002488-26-000018:0005]. AMD reports AI accelerators in its Data Center segment and says it has seen significant demand for them since 2024 [0000002488-26-000018:0024]. In the second quarter of fiscal 2025, AMD recorded about $800 million of inventory and related charges on AMD Instinct MI308 Data Center GPU products because of new U.S. export restrictions on certain semiconductors to China [0000002488-26-000018:0072]. After receiving some licenses to ship MI308 products to certain China-based customers, AMD began shipping in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025 and reversed about $360 million of those charges [0000002488-26-000018:0072].
NVIDIA said its fiscal 2026 revenue growth was driven by data center compute and networking platforms for accelerated computing and AI solutions, and that Blackwell architectures were the majority of its Data Center revenue [0001045810-26-000021:0061]. NVIDIA's two operating segments are "Compute & Networking" and "Graphics" [0001045810-26-000021:0061]. NVIDIA took a $4.5 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal 2026 for H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations, after the U.S. government required a license for H20 exports to China and demand for H20 diminished [0001045810-26-000021:0061]. NVIDIA later generated approximately $60 million in H20 revenue under licenses the U.S. government granted in August 2025 [0001045810-26-000021:0061].
Intel says it missed the shift in compute demand to GPUs optimized for AI workloads and has been unsuccessful to date in becoming a meaningful participant in that market [0000050863-26-000011:0062]. In the DCAI segment, 2025 operating income rose $2.0 billion from 2024, mainly because of lower operating expenses [0000050863-26-000011:0037]. DCAI operating income also benefited from lower Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges than in 2024, while higher DCAI revenue was substantially offset by higher server unit costs [0000050863-26-000011:0037]. Intel recognized Gaudi AI accelerator inventory-related charges of $375 million in 2025 and $922 million in 2024 [0000050863-26-000011:0062].

questions.question: How do NVIDIA, AMD and Intel each address the OECD Pillar Two global minimum tax in their latest 10-Ks, and has any of them quantified its impact?

answer.text:
NVIDIA's FY2026 10-K says that a number of countries where it does business have enacted, or are enacting, elements of the Pillar Two rules, including the recently released "side-by-side" framework, which provides additional safe harbors and coordination mechanisms [0001045810-26-000021:0051]. It warns that such tax laws, or changes to them, may increase tax uncertainty and compliance costs and adversely affect its provision for income taxes, cash tax payments, results of operations and financial condition [0001045810-26-000021:0051]. It also says its tax obligations and effective tax rate could rise as a result of international tax developments, including Pillar One and Pillar Two [0001045810-26-000021:0051]. Its rate reconciliation, with an effective tax rate of 15.1% for the fiscal year ended January 25, 2026, shows no separate Pillar Two line [0001045810-26-000021:0118].
AMD's FY2025 10-K says the OECD is continuing discussions on a global minimum tax ("Pillar One" and "Pillar Two") [0000002488-26-000018:0046]. In January 2026 the OECD released a "side-by-side" package with new safe harbors and an exemption for U.S.-based multinational companies from parts of the global minimum tax framework [0000002488-26-000018:0046]. AMD says these rules are generally favorable to the Company, but each country must adopt them before they are considered enacted for financial accounting purposes [0000002488-26-000018:0046]. AMD says it will keep evaluating the impact on its effective tax rate and cash flows as new guidance becomes available, and it gives no quantified impact [0000002488-26-000018:0046].
Intel's FY2025 10-K lists, among factors that could affect its tax rate, changes in tax laws or their interpretation, including the global implementation of a minimum tax under Pillar Two of the OECD BEPS initiative [0000050863-26-000011:0086]. Its rate reconciliation for the year ended December 27, 2025 shows a global effective tax rate of 98.3% and has no separate Pillar Two line [0000050863-26-000011:0139].

questions.question: How does dependence on external foundries, and on TSMC in particular, differ across NVIDIA, AMD and Intel according to their latest 10-K risk factors?

answer.text:
NVIDIA: NVIDIA says it depends on foundries to manufacture all of its semiconductor wafers, and it does not assemble, test or package its products but contracts with independent subcontractors for that work [0001045810-26-000021:0025]. It names TSMC and Samsung as the foundries it uses to produce wafers [0001045810-26-000021:0012]. Its listed risks include a lack of guaranteed supply of components and capacity, decommitment by suppliers, foundry failure to implement advanced process technologies, and limited number and geographic concentration of suppliers [0001045810-26-000021:0025]. In the excerpts provided, NVIDIA's risk factors do not single out TSMC as a specific dependency in the way AMD's and Intel's do [0001045810-26-000021:0025].
AMD: AMD uses third-party wafer foundries to fabricate the silicon wafers for all of its products [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. It relies on TSMC for all wafers for microprocessor and GPU products at 7 nm or smaller nodes, and primarily on GLOBALFOUNDRIES for those made at nodes larger than 7 nm [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. It also uses TSMC, UMC and Samsung for its programmable logic ICs [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. AMD states that if TSMC cannot manufacture wafers at 7 nm or smaller in sufficient quantities, its business could be materially adversely affected [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. AMD is focusing its 7 nm and lower microprocessor and GPU portfolio on TSMC's processes [0000002488-26-000018:0032]. It does not have long-term commitment contracts with some of its manufacturing suppliers, and those manufacturers could prioritize other customers, including AMD's competitors [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. It has a wafer supply agreement with GF that provides a minimum annual capacity allocation and sets pricing through 2026 [0000002488-26-000018:0029].
Intel: Intel manufactures most of its products in its own facilities, but it has also used third-party foundry capacity, including at TSMC, which it describes as a key foundry competitor [0000050863-26-000011:0018]. Intel expects to keep using TSMC and other third-party foundries for various key tiles in current and future products [0000050863-26-000011:0018]. Some of its most advanced current and future products are or will be either exclusively manufactured by TSMC or reliant upon critical components, including compute die, manufactured by TSMC [0000050863-26-000011:0075]. Because of its disaggregated design, an interruption in TSMC tile supply would leave Intel unable to complete assembly of affected products until it could design and source replacement tiles, likely with a substantial delay [0000050863-26-000011:0063]. If Intel cannot secure a significant external customer for Intel 14A, it may pause or discontinue next-generation node development, and its products business would then become increasingly dependent on third-party foundries, particularly TSMC [0000050863-26-000011:0065]. Intel has no long-term contract with TSMC, and only TSMC and Samsung currently can produce the leading-edge and near-leading-edge nodes it needs [0000050863-26-000011:0065].
In short, AMD is fully fabless and concentrates its leading-edge dependence on TSMC, whereas Intel is mainly an internal manufacturer whose TSMC reliance is growing and tied to its own node strategy [0000002488-26-000018:0029][0000050863-26-000011:0065]. NVIDIA depends on foundries for all its wafers and cites a broader supplier base that includes TSMC and Samsung [0001045810-26-000021:0012][0001045810-26-000021:0025].

Its listed risks include a lack of guaranteed supply of components and capacity, decommitment by suppliers, foundry failure to implement advanced process technologies, and limited number and geographic concentration of suppliers [0001045810-26-000021:0025].
In the excerpts provided, NVIDIA's risk factors do not single out TSMC as a specific dependency in the way AMD's and Intel's do [0001045810-26-000021:0025].
AMD: AMD uses third-party wafer foundries to fabricate the silicon wafers for all of its products [0000002488-26-000018:0029].
It relies on TSMC for all wafers for microprocessor and GPU products at 7 nm or smaller nodes, and primarily on GLOBALFOUNDRIES for those made at nodes larger than 7 nm [0000002488-26-000018:0029].
It also uses TSMC, UMC and Samsung for its programmable logic ICs [0000002488-26-000018:0029].
AMD states that if TSMC cannot manufacture wafers at 7 nm or smaller in sufficient quantities, its business could be materially adversely affected [0000002488-26-000018:0029].
AMD is focusing its 7 nm and lower microprocessor and GPU portfolio on TSMC's processes [0000002488-26-000018:0032].

It does not have long-term commitment contracts with some of its manufacturing suppliers, and those manufacturers could prioritize other customers, including AMD's competitors [0000002488-26-000018:0029].
It has a wafer supply agreement with GF that provides a minimum annual capacity allocation and sets pricing through 2026 [0000002488-26-000018:0029].

Intel: Intel manufactures most of its products in its own facilities, but it has also used third-party foundry capacity, including at TSMC, which it describes as a key foundry competitor [0000050863-26-000011:0018].
Intel expects to keep using TSMC and other third-party foundries for various key tiles in current and future products [0000050863-26-000011:0018].

Some of its most advanced current and future products are or will be either exclusively manufactured by TSMC or reliant upon critical components, including compute die, manufactured by TSMC [0000050863-26-000011:0075].

Because of its disaggregated design, an interruption in TSMC tile supply would leave Intel unable to complete assembly of affected products until it could design and source replacement tiles, likely with a substantial delay [0000050863-26-000011:0063].

If Intel cannot secure a significant external customer for Intel 14A, it may pause or discontinue next-generation node development, and its products business would then become increasingly dependent on third-party foundries, particularly TSMC [0000050863-26-000011:0065].
Intel has no long-term contract with TSMC, and only TSMC and Samsung currently can produce the leading-edge and near-leading-edge nodes it needs [0000050863-26-000011:0065].

In short, AMD is fully fabless and concentrates its leading-edge dependence on TSMC, whereas Intel is mainly an internal manufacturer whose TSMC reliance is growing and tied to its own node strategy [0000002488-26-000018:0029][0000050863-26-000011:0065].
NVIDIA depends on foundries for all its wafers and cites a broader supplier base that includes TSMC and Samsung [0001045810-26-000021:0012][0001045810-26-000021:0025].

questions.question: How concentrated is each company's revenue among its largest customers, as disclosed in the latest 10-K risk factors of NVIDIA, AMD and Intel?

answer.text:
NVIDIA: In its fiscal year 2026 10-K, sales to one direct customer represented 22% of total revenue and sales to another direct customer represented 14% of total revenue, primarily attributable to the Compute & Networking segment [0001045810-26-000021:0036]. NVIDIA also says it generates a significant amount of revenue from a limited number of indirect customers, and it estimates that some of them individually represent 10% or more of its revenue [0001045810-26-000021:0036].
Intel: Its three largest customers collectively accounted for 43% of net revenue in 2025, 45% in 2024 and 40% in 2023 [0000050863-26-000011:0083]. Intel expects a small number of customers to keep accounting for a significant portion of its revenue in the foreseeable future [0000050863-26-000011:0084].
They say AMD depends on a small number of customers for a substantial portion of its business, and it expects a small number of customers to keep accounting for a significant part of its revenue and receivables in the future [0000002488-26-000018:0026].

questions.question: How do NVIDIA, AMD and Intel each describe the role of their software and developer ecosystems in competing for AI and computing workloads, according to their latest 10-Ks?

answer.text:
NVIDIA says its large and growing number of developers and its installed base strengthen its ecosystem and increase the value of its platform for customers [0001045810-26-000021:0005]. It describes a full-stack platform, with the CUDA development platform, the CUDA-X acceleration libraries, AI models, APIs and SDKs, as what makes it more than a chip [0001045810-26-000021:0007]. It reports over 7.5 million developers worldwide using CUDA and its other software tools [0001045810-26-000021:0009]. It also offers paid licenses to NVIDIA AI Enterprise, a suite of enterprise-grade AI software [0001045810-26-000021:0007]. NVIDIA says it seeks strong relationships in the software development community, and its developer program supports AI frameworks, SDKs and APIs optimized for its platforms [0001045810-26-000021:0011]. It also points to partnerships with hundreds of universities and tens of thousands of startups through its Inception program, and to its Deep Learning Institute [0001045810-26-000021:0009].
AMD says it develops software stacks, including development tools, compilers and drivers, for its CPUs, APUs, GPUs and FPGAs, and that it has a comprehensive and open AI software stack supporting diverse AI ecosystems across frameworks, language models and applications [0000002488-26-000018:0004]. It says it continues to invest in software capabilities and the open ecosystem through the AMD ROCm platform, which delivers new features for AI training and inference [0000002488-26-000018:0005]. In 2025, AMD introduced key optimizations and expanded support for frameworks and libraries, improving performance for generative AI workloads and simplifying the developer experience [0000002488-26-000018:0005]. AMD also says it made strategic acquisitions during the year to advance its software capabilities [0000002488-26-000018:0005].
Intel calls its software portfolio a key differentiator for its DCAI business, enabling customers to unlock the full potential of its platforms across cloud, edge and enterprise deployments [0000050863-26-000011:0017]. In 2025, Intel accelerated delivery of data center software and developer tools, focusing on AI, HPC and platform optimization [0000050863-26-000011:0017]. It expanded support for leading AI frameworks, including PyTorch, TensorFlow, Hugging Face and vLLM, optimized for its server CPUs, GPUs and accelerators [0000050863-26-000011:0017].

questions.question: How do NVIDIA, AMD and Intel each characterise the risk of third-party intellectual property infringement claims in their latest 10-Ks, and which of them points to non-practicing entities?

answer.text:
NVIDIA says it is from time to time involved in lawsuits alleging patent infringement or other IP violations by it, its employees or parties it has agreed to indemnify, and that an unfavorable ruling could include significant damages, patent invalidation, indemnification of third parties, lost profits or injunctive relief [0001045810-26-000021:0047]. It adds that infringement claims, regardless of merit, could cause significant costs and divert management and technical personnel [0001045810-26-000021:0047]. If it or an indemnitee cannot obtain a license on acceptable terms, NVIDIA could face substantial liabilities or have to suspend or discontinue manufacture and sale of one or more products, and customer indemnification may increase operating expenses [0001045810-26-000021:0048].
AMD says third parties may bring, or have brought, actions against it or its customers alleging that it infringes, contributes to or induces infringement of others' IP rights, or improperly uses their IP [0000002488-26-000018:0048]. These parties may seek damages (potentially up to treble damages) or an injunction against sale of products, which could force AMD to stop selling some products, raise costs or damage its reputation [0000002488-26-000018:0048]. AMD says it cannot assure that it can obtain necessary licenses on satisfactory terms, that such litigation could be extremely expensive and time-consuming regardless of merit, and that it could have a material adverse effect [0000002488-26-000018:0048].
Intel says third parties assert IP-based claims against it and its products, which could harm its business, and that it is typically engaged in a number of IP disputes [0000050863-26-000011:0080]. Consequences it lists include monetary damages, indemnification payments, royalties, stopping sales of affected products, developing alternative technology, or settlements and licences that may be costly [0000050863-26-000011:0080]. Intel also notes it often indemnifies customers for IP claims against them [0000050863-26-000011:0080]. Its legal proceedings section describes adverse results such as substantial fines and penalties, costly royalty or licensing agreements, or orders preventing it from offering certain products [0000050863-26-000011:0174].
It says it faces claims from non-practicing entities and has seen an increase in assertions and lawsuits by well-funded non-practicing entities, including those funded by third-party investment firms [0000050863-26-000011:0080]. It cites the February 2024 injunction and recall order obtained by R2 Semiconductor, Inc., a non-practicing entity, in the Dusseldorf Regional Court, and names the VLSI and R2 litigation as having resulted in significant adverse judgments and settlements [0000050863-26-000011:0080].

questions.question: According to NVIDIA's FY2026 10-K, how have U.S. export controls affected demand for NVIDIA products outside China, and what has the Chinese government done to discourage purchases of its data center products?

answer.text:
Export controls have in the past and may in the future negatively impact demand for NVIDIA's products and services not only in China but also in other markets such as Europe, Latin America, and Southeast Asia [0001045810-26-000021:0045]. The possibility of additional export controls has negatively impacted, and may in the future negatively impact, demand for NVIDIA's products, benefiting competitors that offer alternatives less likely to be restricted [0001045810-26-000021:0041]. Export controls have already encouraged, and may in the future encourage, customers outside China and other impacted regions to "design-out" certain U.S. semiconductors from their products to reduce compliance burden and risk [0001045810-26-000021:0044][0001045810-26-000021:0045]. They have also encouraged overseas governments to ask customers to buy from NVIDIA's competitors rather than from NVIDIA or other U.S. firms [0001045810-26-000021:0044]. Reduced demand due to export controls has led, and could in the future lead, to excess inventory or related supply charges [0001045810-26-000021:0041]. Export controls could also disrupt NVIDIA's supply chain and distribution channels, affecting its ability to serve demand in markets outside China and for non-data center products [0001045810-26-000021:0041].
On the Chinese government's actions, it has encouraged customers to purchase from NVIDIA's China-based competitors and discouraged customers from purchasing, importing, or using NVIDIA's data center products, including any China-specific product designed to comply with U.S. export controls [0001045810-26-000021:0045][0001045810-26-000021:0015]. After U.S. legislative proposals called for mandatory features in chips, China's government publicly questioned whether the H20 products have built-in vulnerabilities, which discouraged customers from purchasing them [0001045810-26-000021:0044]. An agency of the Chinese government also announced an Action Plan endorsing new standards on compute performance per watt and per memory bandwidth for accelerators used in new and renovated data centers in China [0001045810-26-000021:0045]. In addition, on September 15, 2025, China's antitrust regulators published a preliminary finding that NVIDIA's compliance with U.S. export controls, which required it to offer degraded products to the Chinese market, discriminated unfairly against customers in China and violated the terms of China's approval of the Mellanox acquisition [0001045810-26-000021:0041].

questions.question: What is the status of NVIDIA's licensed H20 and H200 sales to China as described in its FY2026 10-K, including the financial impact and conditions attached to the licenses?

answer.text:
In April 2025, the USG informed NVIDIA that a license is required to export its H20 integrated circuits, and any other circuits achieving the H20's memory bandwidth, interconnect bandwidth, or combination thereof, to China (including Hong Kong and Macau) and D:5 countries, or to companies headquartered or with an ultimate parent there [0001045810-26-000021:0014]. As a result, NVIDIA incurred a $4.5 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 for excess inventory and purchase obligations, because demand for H20 products diminished [0001045810-26-000021:0014][0001045810-26-000021:0062].
In August 2025, the USG granted licenses allowing NVIDIA to ship certain H20 products to certain China-based customers, and NVIDIA generated approximately $60 million in H20 revenue under those licenses [0001045810-26-000021:0014][0001045810-26-000021:0062]. USG officials expressed an expectation that the USG will receive 15% or more of the revenue from licensed sales of NVIDIA's products, but the USG did not publish a regulation codifying that requirement [0001045810-26-000021:0014].
In February 2026, the USG granted a license allowing NVIDIA to ship small amounts of H200 products to specific China-based customers [0001045810-26-000021:0014][0001045810-26-000021:0062]. NVIDIA has not generated any revenue under the H200 licensing program to date and does not yet know whether any imports will be allowed into China [0001045810-26-000021:0014][0001045810-26-000021:0062]. The license requires the H200s to go through an inspection process in the United States before any shipment to the customer, so any H200 shipped under the program will be subject to a 25% tariff upon importation into the United States [0001045810-26-000021:0014][0001045810-26-000021:0062]. If NVIDIA is able to sell licensed products into China, it may not be able to pass along all or any of the tariff to customers, and may face litigation, increased costs and a harmed competitive position [0001045810-26-000021:0014].
More broadly, NVIDIA states that, as of the end of fiscal year 2026, it was effectively foreclosed from competing in China's data center computing market [0001045810-26-000021:0014]. It says it is unable to create and deliver a competitive product for that market that receives approval from both the USG and the Chinese government [0001045810-26-000021:0014].

questions.question: How concentrated was NVIDIA's revenue among direct customers in fiscal year 2026, and what risks does NVIDIA associate with that concentration?

answer.text:
In fiscal year 2026, sales to one direct customer represented 22% of NVIDIA's total revenue and sales to another direct customer represented 14%, all primarily attributable to the Compute & Networking segment [0001045810-26-000021:0067][0001045810-26-000021:0036]. For comparison, in fiscal year 2025 one direct customer represented 12% and two others each represented 11%, and in fiscal year 2024 one direct customer represented 13% [0001045810-26-000021:0067]. NVIDIA says its revenue is concentrated among a limited number of direct and indirect customers and that this trend may continue [0001045810-26-000021:0067].
NVIDIA also generates a significant amount of revenue from a limited number of indirect customers, some individually representing 10% or more of revenue [0001045810-26-000021:0067].
- The loss of any large customer, a significant reduction in purchases by them, an inability to sell to a customer because of U.S. or other countries' trade restrictions, or difficulties in collecting accounts receivable would likely harm its financial condition and results of operations [0001045810-26-000021:0036].
- Most sales are made on a purchase order basis, so customers can generally cancel, change or delay purchase commitments with little notice and without penalty [0001045810-26-000021:0036].
They may also develop their own solutions or buy from competitors [0001045810-26-000021:0036].
- Changes in partners' or customers' business models or ownership can reduce the number of available partners and harm NVIDIA's ability to sell advanced data center systems [0001045810-26-000021:0036].
- Because system designs are increasingly complex, system integrators may be unable to meet key customers' specifications [0001045810-26-000021:0036].
- If end demand increases or finished goods supply is concentrated near a quarter end, system integrators, distributors and channel partners may have limited ability to increase their credit, which could affect the timing and amount of revenue [0001045810-26-000021:0036].
This includes customers' or partners' inability to meet financial commitments or secure financing or infrastructure, significant project delays, and counterparty financial distress or insolvency [0001045810-26-000021:0036].
NVIDIA states that it has not entered into any financing arrangements [0001045810-26-000021:0036].

questions.question: What drove growth in NVIDIA's Compute & Networking segment in the first nine months of fiscal year 2026, broken down between Data Center computing and networking?

answer.text:
The year over year increase in Compute & Networking revenue in the first nine months of fiscal year 2026 was driven by three platform shifts: accelerated computing, powerful AI models, and agentic applications [0001045810-25-000230:0040]. Compute & Networking revenue was $131,828 million for the first nine months of fiscal 2026, up 64% from $80,157 million a year earlier [0001045810-25-000230:0040].
Data Center computing revenue grew 59% year-on-year compared to the first nine months of fiscal year 2025, driven by demand for the Blackwell computing platform [0001045810-25-000230:0040]. Data Center compute revenue was $111,027 million in the first nine months, versus $69,640 million a year earlier [0001045810-25-000230:0032].
Data Center networking revenue grew 105% year-on-year compared to the first nine months of fiscal year 2025 [0001045810-25-000230:0040]. The filing attributes this to the introduction and continued growth of NVLink compute fabric for GB200 and GB300 systems, the growth of XDR InfiniBand products, and adoption of Ethernet for AI solutions [0001045810-25-000230:0040]. Networking revenue was $20,396 million in the first nine months, versus $9,966 million a year earlier [0001045810-25-000230:0032].
Compute & Networking segment operating income rose to $86,139 million in the first nine months, up 49% [0001045810-25-000230:0040]. The filing says this increase was driven by revenue growth, partially offset by a $4.5 billion charge for H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 [0001045810-25-000230:0041].

questions.question: In its Q3 fiscal 2026 10-Q, how does NVIDIA say export controls could affect its gaming and networking products beyond data center GPUs?

answer.text:
For gaming, NVIDIA says the USG already imposed export controls restricting certain gaming GPUs, and that expanding them to additional gaming products may disrupt a significant portion of its supply and distribution chain and negatively impact sales of such products to markets outside China, including the U.S. and Europe [0001045810-25-000230:0063]. It adds that as gaming GPU performance increases over time, export controls may have a greater impact on its ability to compete in markets subject to those controls [0001045810-25-000230:0063]. It also says export controls may disrupt the supply and distribution chain for a substantial portion of its products, which are warehoused in and distributed from Hong Kong [0001045810-25-000230:0063]. More broadly, it says export controls have disrupted and could disrupt its supply chain and distribution channels, affecting its ability to serve demand in markets outside China and for its non-data center products [0001045810-25-000230:0059].
For networking, NVIDIA says export controls restricting its ability to sell data center GPUs may also negatively impact demand for its networking products used in servers containing its GPUs [0001045810-25-000230:0063]. It says the USG may also impose export controls on networking products, such as high-speed network interconnects, to limit the ability of downstream parties to create large clusters for frontier model training [0001045810-25-000230:0063]. Separately, China's antitrust regulators published a preliminary finding on September 15, 2025 that NVIDIA's export-control compliance violated the terms of China's approval of its Mellanox acquisition [0001045810-25-000230:0060]. If regulators conclude NVIDIA failed to fulfill those terms, it could face restrictions or other orders regarding its networking business, products and services [0001045810-25-000230:0060].

questions.question: How did the April 2025 U.S. export license requirement affect AMD's MI308 business over fiscal 2025, according to AMD's FY2025 10-K?

answer.text:
In April 2025, the U.S. government implemented a new license requirement for exporting certain semiconductor products to a D5 country, and to companies headquartered in or with an ultimate parent in such a country, and this restriction impacts AMD Instinct MI308 products [0000002488-26-000018:0042]. As a result, AMD incurred approximately $800 million in inventory and related charges in the second quarter of 2025 [0000002488-26-000018:0042][0000002488-26-000018:0072]. AMD applied for and was granted some licenses that allow it to ship MI308 products to certain China-based customers [0000002488-26-000018:0042]. During the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025, AMD began shipping and reversed approximately $360 million of the earlier charges [0000002488-26-000018:0042][0000002488-26-000018:0072]. For the year ended December 27, 2025, AMD recorded approximately $440 million of net inventory and related charges associated with the export control on MI308 products in cost of sales, and had no export-control-related charges in 2024 or 2023 [0000002488-26-000018:0099]. The Data Center segment's operating income of $3.6 billion in 2025 (versus $3.5 billion in 2024) was partially offset by those approximately $440 million of net charges [0000002488-26-000018:0077].
Looking ahead, AMD says sales of MI308 products into China depend on customer demand, China's import control rules and its ability to obtain licenses [0000002488-26-000018:0042]. In August 2025, U.S. government officials expressed an expectation that the government will receive 15% of the revenue from licensed MI308 sales to China, but the government has not published a regulation establishing such a requirement [0000002488-26-000018:0042][0000002488-26-000018:0043].

questions.question: Which manufacturers does AMD rely on to produce its products, per its FY2025 10-K, and what supply risks does it describe from that reliance?

answer.text:
AMD uses third-party wafer foundries to fabricate the silicon wafers for all of its products [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. It relies on TSMC for all wafers for microprocessor and GPU products at 7 nm or smaller nodes, and primarily on GLOBALFOUNDRIES (GF) for microprocessor and GPU wafers at nodes larger than 7 nm [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. It also uses TSMC, UMC and Samsung for its integrated circuits in the form of programmable logic devices [0000002488-26-000018:0029][0000002488-26-000018:0015]. For assembly, test, mark and pack (ATMP), AMD relies on third-party manufacturers [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. Its two ATMP joint ventures with affiliates of Tongfu Microelectronics, along with SPIL and KYEC, provide ATMP services [0000002488-26-000018:0015]. The majority of its ATMP services come from the ATMP JVs [0000002488-26-000018:0030]. AMD also outsources board-level graphics product manufacturing to third-party manufacturers [0000002488-26-000018:0015].
- AMD cannot guarantee that these manufacturers will meet its near-term or long-term requirements [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. If supply is constrained, it may have to allocate reduced quantities among customers, which could harm customer relationships and its financial condition [0000002488-26-000018:0029].
- If TSMC cannot make wafers at 7 nm or smaller nodes, or its newest IC products, in sufficient quantities, its business could be materially adversely affected [0000002488-26-000018:0029].
- Some suppliers have no long-term commitment contracts with AMD, and many services are bought on a purchase order basis with no minimum quantity beyond the existing order [0000002488-26-000018:0029]. These manufacturers also serve competitors of AMD, and could prioritize other customers' capacity, raise prices on short notice, require onerous prepayments, or reduce or eliminate deliveries [0000002488-26-000018:0029].
- Under its wafer supply agreement with GF, which sets a minimum annual capacity allocation and pricing through 2026, AMD could face excess inventory or higher unit costs if its wafer requirements fall short of the annual purchase target [0000002488-26-000018:0029][0000002488-26-000018:0030].
- Other risks include limited control over delivery schedules, yield, cycle times, quality assurance and price increases, lack of capacity in periods of excess demand, and misappropriation of intellectual property [0000002488-26-000018:0030]. AMD cites an inventory loss in the first quarter of 2024 from an incident at a contract manufacturer [0000002488-26-000018:0030].
- Moving production to new manufacturers could cause delayed product introductions, lower yields or poorer performance, and finding alternative manufacturers could cause significant shipment delays [0000002488-26-000018:0030].
- There is no guarantee that the ATMP JVs will fulfill AMD's long-term ATMP requirements, and late or fluctuating supply from them could result in lost sales [0000002488-26-000018:0030].
- Equipment and materials, including memory, PCBs, interposers, substrates and capacitors, come from a limited number of suppliers or a sole supplier [0000002488-26-000018:0031]. AMD notes an industry-wide memory shortage that has raised memory prices [0000002488-26-000018:0031]. AMD has long-term purchase commitments and prepayment arrangements with some suppliers, so overestimating demand could leave excess inventory and higher production costs [0000002488-26-000018:0031].
- Yield failures at its manufacturers could cause product delivery delays [0000002488-26-000018:0032]. Lower yields could raise per-unit costs, hurt gross margin and force AMD to allocate reduced supply among customers [0000002488-26-000018:0032].

questions.question: How did AMD change its segment reporting in fiscal 2025, and what drove the growth of the Client and Gaming segment that year?

answer.text:
AMD combined its Client and Gaming segments into one reportable segment beginning in the first quarter of fiscal 2025, to align with how it manages its business, and all prior period segment data were retrospectively adjusted [0000002488-26-000018:0070]. As a result, AMD has three reportable segments: Data Center, Client and Gaming, and Embedded [0000002488-26-000018:0006]. The filings say that neither Client nor Gaming qualifies as a separate reportable operating segment, but AMD continues to disclose revenue for each business separately [0000002488-25-000108:0013].
Client and Gaming segment net revenue was $14.6 billion in 2025, up 51% from $9.6 billion in 2024 [0000002488-26-000018:0077]. The overview attributes the growth primarily to strong demand for AMD Ryzen processors, semi-custom game console SoCs and Radeon gaming GPUs [0000002488-26-000018:0070].
Client net revenue was $10.6 billion, up 51% from $7.1 billion, primarily driven by a 31% increase in unit shipments of processors and a 15% increase in average selling price of processors, reflecting strong demand for desktop and mobile Ryzen processors [0000002488-26-000018:0077]. Gaming net revenue was $3.9 billion, up 51% from $2.6 billion, primarily driven by higher semi-custom revenue and strong demand for Radeon gaming GPUs [0000002488-26-000018:0077].
Client and Gaming operating income rose to $2.9 billion in 2025 from $1.2 billion in 2024, primarily due to higher revenue, partially offset by higher cost of sales and operating expenses [0000002488-26-000018:0077].

questions.question: What were AMD's main product and AI strategy milestones in 2025, as described in the FY2025 10-K MD&A?

answer.text:
According to the MD&A, AMD's main priority in 2025 was accelerating growth in the Data Center segment, where demand for its data center AI GPU products was strong as large hyperscale customers, OEMs and ODMs deployed AMD Instinct MI350X Series GPUs [0000002488-26-000018:0071]. AMD advanced its AI GPU roadmap to an annual cadence of leadership for AMD Instinct solutions, beginning with the MI350 Series GPUs in 2025 [0000002488-26-000018:0071]. It also launched the 5th Gen AMD EPYC family of server processors, which it describes as delivering leadership performance for a wide range of data center workloads, including AI [0000002488-26-000018:0071].
The MD&A says AMD expanded its data center portfolio with new networking solutions, including the AMD Pensando "Pollara" 400 AI NICs and "Vulcano" AI NICs [0000002488-26-000018:0071]. It also previewed its Helios AI rack-scale platform, which incorporates all of its data center products (CPUs, GPUs and Networking) [0000002488-26-000018:0071].
In Client and Gaming, AMD brought to market Radeon 9000 Series GPUs and Radeon AI PRO 9700 GPUs based on the AMD RDNA 4 architecture, along with new Ryzen Threadripper 9000 Series processors [0000002488-26-000018:0071]. In its x86 Embedded portfolio, it introduced three new AMD EPYC Embedded series: 9005, 4005 and 2005 [0000002488-26-000018:0071].
AMD also made strategic acquisitions to advance its software capabilities, to scale its photonics and co-packaged optics solutions for next-generation AI systems, and to bring expertise in high-speed inference and reasoning-based AI technologies [0000002488-26-000018:0071]. It brought in multiple AI teams to develop a software ecosystem across its portfolio, and delivered optimizations and expanded framework and library support in the latest AMD ROCm software [0000002488-26-000018:0071][0000002488-26-000018:0072].
In March 2025, AMD completed the acquisition of ZT Systems for $3.2 billion in cash and 8.3 million shares of its common stock [0000002488-26-000018:0072]. In October 2025, it sold the ZT Manufacturing Business to Sanmina for $2.4 billion in cash, subject to certain purchase price adjustments, and 1.2 million shares of Sanmina common stock, while retaining the ZT Design Business [0000002488-26-000018:0072].
In October 2025, AMD entered into a product purchase agreement with OpenAI to deploy 6 gigawatts of AMD GPUs, with the first gigawatt powered by AMD Instinct MI450 series products [0000002488-26-000018:0072]. Concurrently, AMD issued OpenAI a warrant to purchase up to 160 million shares of AMD common stock at an exercise price of $0.01 per share, vesting in tranches based on purchase milestones and AMD stock price targets [0000002488-26-000018:0072]. None of the warrant shares met the vesting or exercise conditions, so the warrant had no impact on the financial statements for the year ended December 27, 2025 [0000002488-26-000018:0072].
Regarding export controls, AMD recorded approximately $800 million of inventory and related charges on AMD Instinct MI308 Data Center GPU products in the second quarter of fiscal 2025 due to new U.S. export restrictions on certain semiconductors to China [0000002488-26-000018:0072]. After being granted some licenses and beginning shipments in the fourth quarter, it reversed approximately $360 million of those charges [0000002488-26-000018:0072].
On results, net revenue increased 34% to $34.6 billion in 2025, and Data Center net revenue was $16.6 billion, up 32% from $12.6 billion in 2024 [0000002488-26-000018:0070].

questions.question: What happened with AMD's acquisition of ZT Systems during fiscal 2025, including the subsequent divestiture of its manufacturing business?

answer.text:
AMD completed the acquisition of ZT Systems on March 31, 2025, for total purchase consideration of $4.4 billion [0000002488-26-000018:0103]. That consideration comprised $3,188 million of cash paid on the Acquisition Date, $860 million for the fair value of 8,335,849 AMD shares issued, and $361 million for the fair value of contingent consideration [0000002488-26-000018:0103]. ZT Systems is a provider of AI and general-purpose compute infrastructure for hyperscale computing companies, and AMD expected the deal to let it deliver end-to-end AI solutions [0000002488-26-000018:0103]. AMD recorded $208 million of goodwill, assigned to the Data Center reporting unit [0000002488-26-000018:0103]. It also recorded $47 million of acquisition-related transaction costs within Marketing, general and administrative expenses in 2025 [0000002488-26-000018:0104].
When it announced the deal in August 2024, AMD disclosed its intent to divest the ZT Manufacturing Business and keep only certain intellectual property and employees (the ZT Design Business) [0000002488-25-000108:0030]. On acquisition, AMD classified the manufacturing business and its related assets and liabilities as held for sale [0000002488-25-000108:0030]. The design business results are included in continuing operations within the Data Center segment and are not material, while the manufacturing business is presented as discontinued operations [0000002488-26-000018:0104].
On May 18, 2025, AMD entered into an equity purchase agreement with Sanmina Corporation to sell the manufacturing business for $3.0 billion in cash and stock, including a contingent payment of up to $450 million [0000002488-25-000108:0030]. AMD completed the sale on October 27, 2025, for $2.4 billion in cash, subject to certain purchase price adjustments, plus 1,151,052 shares of Sanmina common stock [0000002488-26-000018:0104]. At close, AMD received cash of $1.4 billion, net of cash divested and purchase price adjustments, and Sanmina shares valued at $154 million [0000002488-26-000018:0104]. AMD is eligible for up to $450 million of additional cash consideration through 2028 if certain conditions are met (the Sanmina Earn-out) [0000002488-26-000018:0104]. It recorded a Sanmina Earn-out receivable of $332 million within Other non-current assets [0000002488-26-000018:0104]. AMD also entered into a Manufacturing Services Agreement with Sanmina with an initial term of five years [0000002488-26-000018:0104]. Sanmina will be AMD's preferred partner for manufacturing capabilities in building complex AI solutions [0000002488-26-000018:0072].
The change in fair value was $121 million, recorded within Income from discontinued operations [0000002488-26-000018:0104]. The settlement consisted of $300 million in cash and 740,961 AMD shares, completed on October 30, 2025 [0000002488-25-000166:0030].

It also recorded $47 million of acquisition-related transaction costs within Marketing, general and administrative expenses in 2025 [0000002488-26-000018:0104].

When it announced the deal in August 2024, AMD disclosed its intent to divest the ZT Manufacturing Business and keep only certain intellectual property and employees (the ZT Design Business) [0000002488-25-000108:0030].
On acquisition, AMD classified the manufacturing business and its related assets and liabilities as held for sale [0000002488-25-000108:0030].

The design business results are included in continuing operations within the Data Center segment and are not material, while the manufacturing business is presented as discontinued operations [0000002488-26-000018:0104].

On May 18, 2025, AMD entered into an equity purchase agreement with Sanmina Corporation to sell the manufacturing business for $3.0 billion in cash and stock, including a contingent payment of up to $450 million [0000002488-25-000108:0030].
AMD completed the sale on October 27, 2025, for $2.4 billion in cash, subject to certain purchase price adjustments, plus 1,151,052 shares of Sanmina common stock [0000002488-26-000018:0104].
At close, AMD received cash of $1.4 billion, net of cash divested and purchase price adjustments, and Sanmina shares valued at $154 million [0000002488-26-000018:0104].
AMD is eligible for up to $450 million of additional cash consideration through 2028 if certain conditions are met (the Sanmina Earn-out) [0000002488-26-000018:0104].
It recorded a Sanmina Earn-out receivable of $332 million within Other non-current assets [0000002488-26-000018:0104].
AMD also entered into a Manufacturing Services Agreement with Sanmina with an initial term of five years [0000002488-26-000018:0104].
Sanmina will be AMD's preferred partner for manufacturing capabilities in building complex AI solutions [0000002488-26-000018:0072].
The change in fair value was $121 million, recorded within Income from discontinued operations [0000002488-26-000018:0104].
The settlement consisted of $300 million in cash and 740,961 AMD shares, completed on October 30, 2025 [0000002488-25-000166:0030].

questions.question: What caused the declines in AMD's Gaming and Embedded segment revenue in fiscal 2024?

answer.text:
AMD's Gaming net revenue fell 58% to $2.6 billion in 2024, from $6.2 billion in 2023, and the filing says the decrease was primarily due to lower semi-custom product revenue [0000002488-25-000012:0074][0000002488-25-000012:0068].
Embedded net revenue fell 33% to $3.6 billion in 2024, from $5.3 billion in 2023, primarily because of lower demand as customers continued to normalize their inventory levels [0000002488-25-000012:0074].
Customers with higher inventory levels may draw down existing inventory and order less, and Embedded revenue decreased in 2024 as customers continued to normalize inventory [0000002488-25-000012:0025].
In the first quarter of 2024, the filing attributed the Gaming decline to lower semi-custom revenue and lower Radeon GPU sales, and the Embedded decline to customers continuing to manage their inventory levels [0000002488-24-000056:0023].

questions.question: How does AMD's FY2025 10-K describe the status of the AI Diffusion Rule and the risks from potential replacement export rules and tariffs?

answer.text:
In January 2025, BIS issued a final rule, commonly referred to as the "AI Diffusion Rule," that would have imposed new restrictions on the export, reexport and in-country transfer of certain advanced semiconductor devices and technology [0000002488-26-000018:0043]. In May 2025, BIS announced its intention to rescind the rule, publish a regulation formalizing the rescission, and issue replacement rules in the future [0000002488-26-000018:0043].
On replacement rules, AMD says they may limit its ability to engage in certain business transactions, require new export licenses, delay shipments, or necessitate changes in compliance processes and product designs [0000002488-26-000018:0043]. BIS's announced plans also create uncertainty over whether specific products, technologies or software fall within the scope of any new restrictions, and whether BIS will grant licenses in a timely manner or at all [0000002488-26-000018:0043]. Compliance with the planned or existing rules could result in increased costs, disruption of key customer and supplier relationships, loss of competitive positioning in international markets or reputational harm [0000002488-26-000018:0043].
On tariffs, AMD says that implementing or increasing tariffs, trade protection measures or restrictions, or retaliatory actions from foreign governments could result in lost sales and adversely affect its reputation and business [0000002488-26-000018:0043]. The U.S. government has instituted or proposed higher tariffs on imports into the U.S., which could significantly affect AMD's business, particularly the import of products manufactured outside the U.S. [0000002488-26-000018:0043]. Retaliatory actions could bring tariffs or other restrictions on AMD's products, and customers' costs may rise or their sales may fall, so demand for AMD's products may decline, which could reduce revenue and lead to inventory impairment charges [0000002488-26-000018:0043]. For instance, tariffs on hardware required for data centers could raise customers' costs and lead them to delay or cancel AI infrastructure investments [0000002488-26-000018:0043][0000002488-26-000018:0044].

questions.question: How did Intel change its approach to deploying manufacturing capital in 2025, and what does its FY2025 10-K say would happen to Intel 14A if it cannot secure a significant external customer?

answer.text:
In 2025, Intel moved to a more disciplined capital deployment strategy, better aligning new investments and key project milestones with market demand, after making substantial investments from 2021 through 2024 in technology development, manufacturing facility shells and advanced production tools [0000050863-26-000011:0023]. As part of this, it initiated the consolidation of its Costa Rican assembly and test operations into larger existing sites in Vietnam and Malaysia, expected to be completed by the end of 2026 [0000050863-26-000011:0023]. It also slowed the pace of construction for its new Ohio fab and discontinued planned expansions in Germany (fab) and Poland (assembly and test) [0000050863-26-000011:0023]. Intel describes these actions as reflecting a focus on deploying capital in coordination with tangible milestones and scaling capacity as needed [0000050863-26-000011:0034].
If Intel cannot secure a significant external customer for Intel 14A, it may pause or discontinue its pursuit of Intel 14A and successor leading-edge nodes [0000050863-26-000011:0065]. The filing says it would also face the prospect that developing and manufacturing Intel 14A and successor nodes would not be economical, and it may pause or discontinue various manufacturing expansion projects [0000050863-26-000011:0034]. In that event, Intel would expect over time to shift manufacturing to third-party foundries, particularly TSMC, as it develops products for nodes beyond Intel 18A and Intel 18A-P [0000050863-26-000011:0008].
These include significant material impairments of foundry assets, a likely discontinuation of the new Ohio fabs, possible loss of eligibility for government incentives and possible repayment of amounts already received, potential substantial additional payments to its SCIP partners, and possible loss of talent [0000050863-26-000011:0066]. The filing adds that Intel has been unsuccessful to date in securing any significant external foundry customers for any of its nodes, and that its prospects for securing one for Intel 14A are uncertain [0000050863-26-000011:0065]. If it did discontinue Intel 14A, Intel expects a majority of its products would continue to be manufactured in its own facilities, using nodes up to Intel 18A-P, through at least 2030 [0000050863-26-000011:0034].

questions.question: What were the key terms of Intel's August 2025 agreement with the U.S. Department of Commerce, as described in its FY2025 10-K?

answer.text:
On August 22, 2025, Intel entered into a Warrant and Common Stock Agreement with the U.S. Department of Commerce (DOC) to support the continued expansion of U.S. semiconductor technology and manufacturing leadership [0000050863-26-000011:0030].
Under the agreement, the U.S. government agreed to make disbursements consisting of $5.7 billion from the acceleration of certain disbursements under an amendment to the November 2024 Direct Funding Agreement under the CHIPS Act, plus $3.2 billion of disbursements under the Secure Enclave program, to be made as Intel performs on its commitments [0000050863-26-000011:0127].
As compensation, Intel agreed to issue to the DOC up to 433 million shares of common stock, of which 275 million would be issued on the closing date and 159 million would be issued into escrow to be released as Secure Enclave disbursements are received [0000050863-26-000011:0127]. Intel also agreed to issue warrants to purchase up to 241 million shares at $20.00 per share if it were to cease to directly or indirectly own at least 51% of its foundry business [0000050863-26-000011:0127].
The DOC also agreed that, to the maximum extent permissible under applicable law, Intel's obligations under the DFA would be considered discharged, other than with respect to Secure Enclave [0000050863-26-000011:0127].
On that date Intel and the DOC amended the DFA to remove the prior project milestone requirements and certain other conditions to disbursements, Intel received the remaining $5.7 billion of DFA disbursements, and it issued the 275 million shares, the warrants and the 159 million escrowed shares [0000050863-26-000011:0127]. The amendment also removed substantially all other requirements under the agreement other than those required by law, including those tied to the $2.3 billion previously received and recognized as government incentives [0000050863-26-000011:0030].
The escrowed shares are released to the U.S. government on a $20.00 per share basis as Intel receives the $3.2 billion of Secure Enclave disbursements, and 3 million had been released as of December 27, 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0030]. Secure Enclave proceeds received after the agreement's effective date are attributed as equity and are not subject to Intel's grant accounting policy [0000050863-26-000011:0133].
Intel's accounting conclusion for the agreement was adjusted after consultation with the SEC staff, which concluded in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2025, and Intel concluded the adjustments were immaterial to its Q3 2025 Form 10-Q financial statements [0000050863-26-000011:0030]. In 2025, interest and other, net, included a $1.8 billion net loss from the change in fair value of the derivative liability for the Escrowed Shares [0000050863-26-000011:0046].

questions.question: What did Intel's 2025 Restructuring Plan aim to do, and what restructuring and related charges did Intel record in 2025?

answer.text:
Intel's 2025 Restructuring Plan was implemented to lower expenses, streamline the organizational structure and reduce management layers across functions, while reallocating resources toward the core client and server businesses by reducing investment in lower-priority programs and initiatives [0000050863-26-000011:0032]. These headcount reductions cut Intel's core workforce by approximately 15% by the end of fiscal 2025, compared with the Q2 2025 ending headcount [0000050863-26-000011:0032].
In 2025, Intel recognized restructuring charges of $2.2 billion, consisting primarily of charges from initiating and deploying the 2025 Restructuring Plan and from substantially completing the 2024 Restructuring Plan [0000050863-26-000011:0032]. Of this, cash-based employee severance and related employee exit charges were $1.8 billion, and non-cash asset impairment charges were $474 million, resulting from the exit of certain non-core lines of business and the consolidation and exit of certain real estate properties [0000050863-26-000011:0032].
The restructuring and other charges table shows fiscal 2025 totals of $2,191 million, made up of $1,790 million of employee severance and benefit arrangements, $(121) million of litigation charges and other, and $522 million of asset impairment charges [0000050863-26-000011:0044]. The employee severance line includes net charges of $1.5 billion for the 2025 Restructuring Plan and $281 million for the 2024 Restructuring Plan and other actions [0000050863-26-000011:0044]. The $522 million of asset impairment charges consisted primarily of non-cash charges associated with the 2025 Restructuring Plan [0000050863-26-000011:0044]. The cumulative cost of the 2025 Restructuring Plan as of December 27, 2025 was $2.0 billion, and Intel expects total charges of approximately $2.2 billion under the plan [0000050863-26-000011:0135].
Separately, Intel recorded non-cash charges of $950 million, net of certain items, to cost of sales in 2025 for accelerated depreciation and impairment of certain manufacturing assets that were determined to have no remaining operational use, which affected the Intel Foundry segment [0000050863-26-000011:0032].

questions.question: How did Intel describe Intel Foundry's strategy, process technology offerings and competitors in its FY2024 10-K?

answer.text:
Strategy: Intel described Intel Foundry as comprising technology development, manufacturing and foundry services, seeking to deliver the best systems foundry capabilities to support Intel Products and external customers [0000050863-25-000009:0030]. Intel said it expects its factories to keep mostly producing its own products for many years, while aiming to become a major provider of semiconductor manufacturing solutions for third parties [0000050863-25-000009:0030]. Its own product volume provides the scale needed for leading-edge foundry operations and helps derisk the offering for third-party customers [0000050863-25-000009:0030]. Intel plans to establish Intel Foundry as an independent subsidiary, which it expects to give clearer separation for foundry customers and suppliers and more flexibility to evaluate separate funding and capital structures [0000050863-25-000009:0031]. Intel said it believes it is one of only three manufacturers pursuing 2nm lithography [0000050863-25-000009:0030]. It plans to differentiate its foundry through leading-edge packaging and process technology, committed capacity in the US and Europe, and an IP portfolio that will include x86 cores [0000050863-25-000009:0007]. The foundry offering has four components: wafer fabrication, packaging, chiplets, and software and services [0000050863-25-000009:0007].
Process technology offerings: Intel expects volume production on its 2nm node, Intel 18A, in 2025 [0000050863-25-000009:0031]. The process technologies expected to be available to external customers include Intel 18A with RibbonFET (gate-all-around) and PowerVia (back-side power delivery), Intel 3 using EUV lithography, the established Intel 7 and Intel 16, and a new 12nm process being developed with UMC [0000050863-25-000009:0031]. Intel also announced Intel 14A as an extension of its roadmap beyond Intel 18A [0000050863-25-000009:0031]. Intel described Intel 14A as its third advanced process technology offering to external customers, in active development with performance-per-watt and density improvements over Intel 18A [0000050863-25-000009:0013]. Intel 3 is optimized for data center products [0000050863-25-000009:0012]. Foundry offerings also include advanced assembly and test and packaging technologies [0000050863-25-000009:0031].
Competitors: Intel named TSMC, Samsung, Global Foundries, UMC and SMIC as competitors, primarily foundries with fabrication plants based mainly in Asia [0000050863-25-000009:0031]. It said it competes with TSMC and Samsung in the advanced process technology marketplace [0000050863-25-000009:0031]. In its risk factors, Intel said it has limited experience in the highly competitive, capital-intensive third-party foundry business and will face intense competition from these established players [0000050863-25-000009:0048]. It also said the hurdles to its foundry strategy make it highly risky and its success highly uncertain [0000050863-25-000009:0050].

Yeary as Interim Executive Chair of the Board, David Zinsner as Interim Co-Chief Executive Officer (also Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer), and Michelle Johnston Holthaus as Interim Co-Chief Executive Officer and Chief Executive Officer of Intel Products [0000050863-25-000009:0174].

questions.question: Where does the European Commission competition case against Intel stand in its FY2025 10-K, and how much has Intel accrued for it?

answer.text:
The European Commission found in 2009 that Intel had used unfair business practices, imposed a €1.1 billion fine that Intel paid in the third quarter of 2009, and Intel appealed [0000050863-26-000011:0171]. In January 2022 the General Court annulled the EC's 2009 findings on rebates and the €1.1 billion fine, which was returned to Intel in February 2022, but it did not annul the finding that Intel made payments to prevent sales of specific rival products [0000050863-26-000011:0171]. In April 2022 the EC appealed the rebate findings to the Court of Justice, and in October 2024 the Court of Justice dismissed that appeal and upheld the General Court's judgment [0000050863-26-000011:0171].
In September 2023 the EC imposed a €376 million ($401 million) fine based on the finding about payments to prevent sales of rival products [0000050863-26-000011:0172]. Intel appealed, and in December 2025 the General Court reduced the fine to €237 million ($277 million) [0000050863-26-000011:0172]. Intel may appeal that decision to the Court of Justice [0000050863-26-000011:0172].
As of December 27, 2025, Intel had accrued approximately $311 million for the fine, including foreign currency revaluation effects and accrued interest [0000050863-26-000011:0172][0000050863-26-000011:0171]. Intel says it cannot reasonably estimate any potential loss or range of losses above that amount, given the procedural posture and nature of the proceedings [0000050863-26-000011:0172].
The fine remains unpaid on appeal, and a third party guarantees Intel's obligation [0000050863-26-000011:0136]. Intel funded the guarantee in 2025 by depositing $340 million in legally restricted accounts [0000050863-26-000011:0136]. The reduction of the previously accrued fine produced a $163 million benefit in 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0136].

questions.question: What is the current status of the securities class action and related derivative lawsuits against NVIDIA over cryptocurrency-mining demand, per its FY2026 10-K?

answer.text:
The securities class action, In Re NVIDIA Corporation Securities Litigation, was dismissed by the district court on March 2, 2021, and the plaintiffs appealed to the Ninth Circuit [0001045810-26-000021:0115]. On August 25, 2023, a majority of a three-judge Ninth Circuit panel affirmed in part and reversed in part the dismissal [0001045810-26-000021:0115]. The Supreme Court dismissed NVIDIA's writ of certiorari as improvidently granted on December 11, 2024, and issued judgment on January 13, 2025 [0001045810-26-000021:0116]. On February 20, 2025, the Ninth Circuit's judgment took effect and the case was remanded to the district court for further proceedings [0001045810-26-000021:0116].
The derivative lawsuit in the Northern District of California (In re NVIDIA Corporation Consolidated Derivative Litigation) was stayed pending the securities appeal and administratively closed on February 22, 2022 [0001045810-26-000021:0116]. The court said it would reopen the case once the appeal is resolved, and the case had not yet been reopened [0001045810-26-000021:0116].
On March 7, 2025, the district court adopted the parties' stipulation to extend the stay until the final and complete resolution of the securities class action [0001045810-26-000021:0116].
Huang, was filed on October 30, 2023 [0001045810-26-000021:0117]. On August 11, 2025, the court granted a stipulation to voluntarily dismiss plaintiff City of Westland Police and Fire Retirement System with prejudice [0001045810-26-000021:0117]. The matter is stayed pending final resolution of the securities class action [0001045810-26-000021:0117].
As of January 25, 2026, NVIDIA had no accrued contingent liabilities for these proceedings, because it believes liabilities, while reasonably possible, are not probable [0001045810-26-000021:0117]. It also states that any possible loss or range of loss cannot be reasonably estimated at this time [0001045810-26-000021:0117]. The risk factors describe the company as still defending the securities class action [0001045810-26-000021:0052].

questions.question: What risks does NVIDIA's FY2026 10-K associate with its acquisitions and strategic investments, including its planned OpenAI deal?

answer.text:
NVIDIA says acquisitions and investments involve significant challenges and risks, and could impair its ability to grow its business, develop new products or sell its products, and ultimately hurt its financial results [0001045810-26-000021:0034]. Pursuing one transaction may limit its ability to enter into others [0001045810-26-000021:0034]. If it cannot complete acquisitions on time, including because of delays in regulatory approvals, it may be unable to pursue other transactions, may not retain critical talent from the target, and technology may evolve and make the acquisition less attractive [0001045810-26-000021:0034]. Regulators could also impose conditions that reduce the value of its acquisitions, and if its perceived ability to complete acquisitions is harmed, future ones may be more difficult, complex or expensive [0001045810-26-000021:0034].
Its investments in companies could create volatility in its results, generating realized and unrealized gains or losses, and it could lose up to the full value of the investments [0001045810-26-000021:0034].
