questions.question: Why did NVIDIA's gross margin decrease in fiscal year 2026?

answer.text:
NVIDIA's gross margin fell to 71.1% in fiscal year 2026 from 75.0% in fiscal year 2025 [0001045810-26-000021:0068]. The 10-K gives two reasons: the business model moved from offering Hopper HGX systems to Blackwell full-scale datacenter solutions, and a $4.5 billion charge for H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 [0001045810-26-000021:0068][0001045810-26-000021:0063].
Demand for H20 diminished as a result [0001045810-26-000021:0061].
The net effect on gross margin was an unfavorable 2.6% in fiscal year 2026 and 2.3% in fiscal year 2025 [0001045810-26-000021:0068].
First-quarter gross margin was 60.5%, down mainly because of the H20 charge and the initial ramp of more sophisticated Data Center systems [0001045810-25-000116:0034]. In the second quarter, the filing attributes the year-over-year decline to Blackwell revenue consisting primarily of full-scale datacenter systems rather than Hopper HGX systems [0001045810-25-000209:0040].

questions.question: In calendar 2024, how did data center revenue growth compare between AMD (fiscal 2024) and NVIDIA (fiscal 2025), and what drove it at each company?

answer.text:
AMD's Data Center net revenue was $12.6 billion in fiscal 2024, up 94% from $6.5 billion in 2023 [0000002488-25-000012:0068]. AMD attributed the increase primarily to higher sales of AMD Instinct GPUs and AMD EPYC CPUs [0000002488-25-000012:0073]. Demand for its Data Center AI accelerator products was very strong, led by large hyperscale cloud customers deploying the AMD Instinct MI300X GPU accelerators [0000002488-25-000012:0068].
NVIDIA's Data Center revenue for fiscal year 2025 (ended January 26, 2025) was up 142% from a year ago [0001045810-25-000023:0064]. NVIDIA said the growth was driven by demand for its Hopper architecture accelerated computing platform, used for large language models, recommendation engines and generative AI applications [0001045810-25-000023:0064]. It also began shipping production systems of the Blackwell architecture in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025 [0001045810-25-000023:0064].
Both were driven by demand for GPU-based AI accelerators, and AMD's growth also drew on EPYC server CPUs [0000002488-25-000012:0068][0001045810-25-000023:0064].

questions.question: How did AMD's Data Center segment and Intel's DCAI segment revenue change in fiscal 2025 versus 2024, and what drove each?

answer.text:
AMD's Data Center net revenue was $16.6 billion in 2025, up 32% from $12.6 billion in 2024 [0000002488-26-000018:0077]. The filing says the increase was primarily driven by strong demand for AMD EPYC processors and AMD Instinct GPU accelerators [0000002488-26-000018:0077]. The segment table shows $16,635 million in 2025 against $12,579 million in 2024 [0000002488-26-000018:0076].
Intel's DCAI revenue was $16,919 million in 2025 against $16,125 million in 2024 [0000050863-26-000011:0035]. That is an increase of $794 million, or 5% [0000050863-26-000011:0036][0000050863-26-000011:0042]. Intel says the increase was primarily driven by higher server revenue from higher hyperscale customer-related demand, which contributed to a 9% increase in server volume [0000050863-26-000011:0036]. Server ASPs fell 4%, primarily because of pricing actions taken mainly in the first half of 2025 and a higher mix of lower core count products, both driven by a competitive environment, partly offset by higher ASPs in the second half of 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0036]. Other DCAI product revenue also rose on higher networking customer-related demand [0000050863-26-000011:0036]. Intel also said DCAI revenue was limited in Q4 2025 by available supply because of wafer fabrication supply constraints, primarily on its Intel 7 and Intel 3 process nodes [0000050863-26-000011:0036].

questions.question: What charges did NVIDIA and AMD each record from the April 2025 U.S. export license requirements on their China-bound data center GPUs, and how did those charges show up in their quarterly results?

answer.text:
NVIDIA recorded a $4.5 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 for H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations, after the U.S. government told it on April 9, 2025 that a license was required to export H20 integrated circuits to China and D:5 countries [0001045810-25-000116:0028][0001045810-25-000116:0048]. NVIDIA said the charge was less than it first anticipated because it was able to re-use certain materials [0001045810-25-000116:0028]. Its H20 sales were $4.6 billion in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026, prior to the new export licensing requirements [0001045810-25-000116:0028]. NVIDIA also said the H20 licensing requirements affected its current revenue and would negatively affect its future revenue [0001045810-25-000116:0028].
AMD said the April 2025 license requirement affects its AMD Instinct MI308 products, and that it incurred approximately $800 million in inventory and related charges in the second quarter of 2025 [0000002488-25-000166:0063][0000002488-25-000108:0065]. In the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025, AMD began shipping products after being granted some licenses and reversed approximately $360 million of the charges recorded earlier in the year [0000002488-26-000018:0042].

AMD's fiscal 2025 10-K discloses that in October 2025 it entered into a product purchase agreement with OpenAI OpCo, LLC to deploy 6 gigawatts of AMD GPUs, with the first gigawatt of capacity powered by AMD Instinct MI450 series products [0000002488-26-000018:0006][0000002488-26-000018:0072]. The filing describes this as a multiyear strategic partnership [0000002488-26-000018:0005]. Alongside the agreement, AMD issued OpenAI a warrant to purchase up to 160 million shares of AMD common stock at an exercise price of $0.01 per share [0000002488-26-000018:0072]. Each vested tranche is also subject to other technical and commercial conditions before exercise, and the warrant is exercisable through October 5, 2030 [0000002488-26-000018:0072].
On progress, the filing states that none of the warrant shares had met the vesting or exercise conditions, and the warrant had no impact on AMD's financial statements for the year ended December 27, 2025 [0000002488-26-000018:0072].
They mention only that AI model makers are among NVIDIA's customers, without naming OpenAI [0001045810-26-000021:0007].

questions.question: How did client CPU revenue trend at AMD and at Intel in fiscal 2025, and what explains the different directions?

answer.text:
Client net revenue was $10.6 billion in 2025, up 51% from $7.1 billion in 2024 [0000002488-26-000018:0077]. AMD attributes the increase mainly to a 31% rise in unit shipments of processors and a 15% rise in average selling price, reflecting strong demand for its desktop and mobile Ryzen processors [0000002488-26-000018:0077]. In Q1 2025, AMD's client revenue was up 68% from the prior year period, driven by a 43% rise in average selling price and a 23% rise in unit shipments [0000002488-25-000047:0024].
Client revenue (notebook and desktop) was $27.6 billion in 2025, down $1.1 billion from 2024 [0000050863-26-000011:0036]. Intel attributes the decline mainly to lower client volume, which stemmed from incremental customer incentives offered to certain customers in the first half of 2024 and from customer inventory reductions in 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0036]. Intel's client ASPs in 2025 were roughly flat with 2024 [0000050863-26-000011:0036]. Those incentives contributed approximately $1.6 billion to Intel's revenue in Q1 2024 and were insignificant in Q1 2025 [0000050863-25-000074:0041].
Client volume decreased in Q4 2025 because market demand exceeded available supply, owing to Intel Foundry wafer fabrication constraints, primarily on the Intel 7 process node [0000050863-26-000011:0036]. Intel expects these constraints to persist into 2026, with the most severe impact in Q1 2026 [0000050863-26-000011:0036]. Higher Q3 2025 client volumes driven by higher demand partly offset the full-year decrease [0000050863-26-000011:0036].
In short, the excerpts show AMD's client revenue growing on higher unit shipments and prices amid strong Ryzen demand, while Intel's declined on lower volume tied to a prior-year incentive comparison, inventory reductions and supply constraints, with flat pricing [0000002488-26-000018:0077][0000050863-26-000011:0036].

questions.question: After the U.S. government granted licenses in 2025 for some China-bound data center GPUs, what did NVIDIA (fiscal 2026 10-K) and AMD (fiscal 2025 10-K) report about licensed shipments and the U.S. government's expected revenue share?

answer.text:
NVIDIA said that in August 2025 the U.S. government granted licenses allowing it to ship certain H20 products to certain China-based customers, and that it generated approximately $60 million in H20 revenue under those licenses [0001045810-26-000021:0014][0001045810-26-000021:0062]. NVIDIA also said U.S. government officials expressed an expectation that the government will receive 15% or more of the revenue from licensed sales of its products, but the government did not publish a regulation codifying that requirement [0001045810-26-000021:0014]. Separately, in February 2026 the government granted a license for small amounts of H200 products to specific China-based customers, but NVIDIA had not generated any revenue under that program and did not yet know whether imports would be allowed into China [0001045810-26-000021:0014].
AMD said it applied for and was granted some licenses allowing it to ship MI308 products to certain China-based customers [0000002488-26-000018:0042]. During the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025, AMD began shipping products and reversed approximately $360 million of the roughly $800 million in inventory and related charges recorded earlier in the year [0000002488-26-000018:0042][0000002488-26-000018:0072]. AMD said that in August 2025 U.S. government officials expressed an expectation that the government will receive 15% of the revenue from licensed MI308 sales to China, but the government had not published a regulation establishing such a requirement [0000002488-26-000018:0042][0000002488-26-000018:0072]. AMD added that sales of MI308 products into China depend on customer demand, China's import control rules and its ability to obtain licenses [0000002488-26-000018:0042].

questions.question: AMD's fiscal 2025 10-K names Altera as a competitor. What happened to Intel's ownership of Altera in 2025, and how does Intel now account for it?

answer.text:
On April 14, 2025, Intel signed an agreement to sell 51% of Altera's issued and outstanding common stock, and Altera was then a wholly owned subsidiary [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. Intel completed that sale on September 12, 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0145].
Its results were included in Intel's "all other" category through September 11, 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0013].
It is classified within equity investments in the Consolidated Balance Sheets [0000050863-26-000011:0146]. As of December 27, 2025, the carrying value of this investment was $3.2 billion and Intel's ownership interest was 48% [0000050863-26-000011:0145].
The governance structure does not allow Intel to direct the activities that most significantly affect Altera's economic performance [0000050863-26-000011:0146].
The divestiture produced a pre-tax gain of $5.6 billion, recognized within interest and other, net [0000050863-26-000011:0031]. About $2.1 billion of that gain came from remeasuring the retained investment to fair value at the closing date [0000050863-26-000011:0031].
answer.raw_text:
STATUS: answered

The excerpts here are all from Intel's filings, so I can't confirm the AMD claim in the question. They do cover Intel's side. On April 14, 2025, Intel signed an agreement to sell 51% of Altera's issued and outstanding common stock, and Altera was then a wholly owned subsidiary [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. Intel completed that sale on September 12, 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0145].

Altera was deconsolidated from Intel's Consolidated Financial Statements effective September 12, 2025. Its results were included in Intel's "all other" category through September 11, 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0013].

Intel retained a 49% minority interest, which it accounts for under the equity method. It is classified within equity investments in the Consolidated Balance Sheets [0000050863-26-000011:0146]. As of December 27, 2025, the carrying value of this investment was $3.2 billion and Intel's ownership interest was 48% [0000050863-26-000011:0145].

Intel concluded that Altera is a variable interest entity for which it is not the primary beneficiary. The governance structure does not allow Intel to direct the activities that most significantly affect Altera's economic performance [0000050863-26-000011:0146].

The divestiture produced a pre-tax gain of $5.6 billion, recognized within interest and other, net [0000050863-26-000011:0031]. About $2.1 billion of that gain came from remeasuring the retained investment to fair value at the closing date [0000050863-26-000011:0031].

questions.question: What did AMD say drove its Data Center segment revenue growth in the second quarter of 2024, and how did the drivers and segment profitability differ in the second quarter of 2025?

answer.text:
For the second quarter of 2024 (three months ended June 29, 2024), AMD reported Data Center net revenue of $2.8 billion, up 115% from $1.3 billion in the prior year period, primarily driven by the steep ramp of AMD Instinct GPU shipments and strong growth in 4th Gen AMD EPYC CPU sales [0000002488-24-000123:0026]. Data Center operating income for that quarter was $743 million, compared with $147 million a year earlier, and the increase was primarily driven by higher revenue [0000002488-24-000123:0026].
For the second quarter of 2025 (three months ended June 28, 2025), Data Center net revenue was $3.2 billion, up 14% from $2.8 billion in the prior year period, and the increase was primarily driven by growth in AMD EPYC CPU sales [0000002488-25-000108:0033]. The Instinct GPU ramp is not cited as a driver in the 2025 explanation [0000002488-25-000108:0033].
On profitability, Data Center recorded an operating loss of $155 million in the second quarter of 2025, compared with operating income of $743 million in the prior year period [0000002488-25-000108:0033]. AMD attributed the decrease primarily to approximately $800 million of inventory and related charges associated with the U.S. government export control on AMD Instinct MI308 GPU products, and to higher R&D expense [0000002488-25-000108:0033].

Server volume decreased 22% in Q2 2024 because of lower demand in a competitive environment and a higher mix of high core count products [0000050863-24-000124:0040]. Server ASPs increased 23% in Q2 2024, primarily due to a lower mix of hyperscale customer-related revenue and a higher mix of high core count products [0000050863-24-000124:0040].
So volume went from a 22% decline in Q2 2024 to a 13% increase in Q2 2025, while server ASPs went from a 23% increase to an 8% decrease [0000050863-24-000124:0040][0000050863-25-000109:0044]. Intel pointed to hyperscale demand as supporting volume in Q2 2025 and to competitive pricing as pressuring ASPs [0000050863-25-000109:0044]. In Q2 2024, a lower hyperscale mix and a higher mix of high core count products had lifted ASPs [0000050863-24-000124:0040].

questions.question: Intel's fiscal 2024 10-K disclosed capital expenditure commitments for 2025. How did Intel's actual 2025 additions to property, plant and equipment, reported in the fiscal 2025 10-K, compare with that commitment and with 2024 spending, and how did Intel explain the change in investing cash flows?

The fiscal 2024 10-K said that, as of December 28, 2024, Intel had commitments for capital expenditures of $14.0 billion for 2025 [0000050863-25-000009:0042]. Separately, Intel reported additions to property, plant and equipment of $3,026 million in 2025 within financing activities, compared with $1,178 million in 2024 [0000050863-26-000011:0103].
Net cash used for investing activities was $14,821 million in 2025 versus $18,256 million in 2024 [0000050863-26-000011:0050]. Intel said the decrease was primarily due to lower capital expenditures, higher proceeds from the divestitures of its Altera and NAND memory businesses, and other cash-favorable investing activity [0000050863-26-000011:0050]. These favorable effects were partially offset by higher purchases of short-term investments net of sales and maturities, lower sales of equity investments, and lower proceeds from capital-related government incentives [0000050863-26-000011:0050].

questions.question: How did Intel Foundry's third-quarter operating loss move from Q3 2023 to Q3 2024 to Q3 2025, and what were the main drivers of each change?

answer.text:
Intel Foundry's operating loss was $1.4 billion in Q3 2023 [0000050863-24-000149:0047]. It widened to $5.8 billion in Q3 2024 [0000050863-24-000149:0047], then narrowed to $2.3 billion in Q3 2025 [0000050863-25-000179:0056].
The Q3 2024 loss is shown as $5,844 million in the Q3 2024 filing [0000050863-24-000149:0047]. The Q3 2025 filing's comparative table shows $5,799 million for the same quarter [0000050863-25-000179:0055].
- The largest driver was $3,095 million of higher period charges for non-cash impairments and accelerated depreciation on certain manufacturing assets, a substantial majority of which related to the Intel 7 process node [0000050863-24-000149:0047].
- Lower intersegment product and services profit added $976 million to the loss, primarily due to lower intersegment ASPs, lower intersegment samples and lower external revenue [0000050863-24-000149:0047].
- Higher operating expenses added $297 million, primarily from increased investments in process technology [0000050863-24-000149:0047].
- Higher period charges, primarily for factory start-up costs, added $136 million [0000050863-24-000149:0047].
- "Other" items offset $67 million [0000050863-24-000149:0047].
- The loss was primarily reduced by the absence of the $3.1 billion of non-cash asset impairment and accelerated depreciation charges recognized in Q3 2024, a substantial majority of which related to the Intel 7 process node [0000050863-25-000179:0056].
- Q3 2025 also benefited from $421 million of lower operating expenses, primarily due to lower payroll-related expenditures from headcount reductions under the 2025 and 2024 Restructuring Plans and various cost-reduction measures [0000050863-25-000179:0056].

The Q1 2025 10-Q says client revenue (notebook and desktop combined) was $6.5 billion in Q1 2025, down $599 million from Q1 2024, primarily because of lower client volume that resulted from incremental customer incentives offered to certain customers in Q1 2024 [0000050863-25-000074:0037]. Client ASPs in Q1 2025 were roughly flat with Q1 2024 [0000050863-25-000074:0037]. The filing adds that CCG revenue fell 8% mainly on lower client volumes tied to the absence of those incentives [0000050863-25-000074:0041]. Incentives contributed approximately $1.6 billion to revenue in Q1 2024 and were insignificant in Q1 2025 [0000050863-25-000074:0041].

The Q1 2024 10-Q reported that notebook revenue was $4.7 billion, up $1.3 billion from Q1 2023, and desktop revenue was $2.5 billion, up $582 million from Q1 2023 [0000050863-24-000076:0034]. Notebook volume rose 39% and desktop volume rose 29% in Q1 2024 as customer inventory levels normalized compared with higher levels in Q1 2023 [0000050863-24-000076:0034]. Notebook and desktop ASPs were roughly flat with Q1 2023 [0000050863-24-000076:0034]. CCG revenue in Q1 2024 increased 31% from Q1 2023 [0000050863-24-000076:0039]. Incentives contributed approximately $1.6 billion to revenue in Q1 2024, compared with approximately $900 million in Q1 2023 [0000050863-24-000076:0039].
